title: Sow in the Morn Thy Seed
description: Sow in the Morn Thy Seed in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 540, “The Sower”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sow in the morn thy seed, At eve hold not thy hand; To doubt and fear give thou no_ heed, Broad-cast it o'er the land! Be-side all wa-ters sow, The high-way fur-rows stock, Drop it where thorns and this-tles grow, Drop it up-on the rock!

lines: Sow in the morn thy seed,
At eve hold not thy hand;
To doubt and fear give thou no heed,
Drop it where thorns and thistles grow,
O'er hill and dale and plain 'tis found,
The tender blade, the stalk, the ear,
And the full corn at length.
Thou canst not toil in vain;
Cold, heat, and moist and dry,
Shall foster and mature the grain
The day of God, shall come,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
